Hi Samantha —

Thanks for sharing the questionnaire and the SLA preferences. I’ve reviewed the VSA and provided initial answers inline in the attached VSA_Responses_Amaya.xlsx (summary below). We’ll surface any items that require legal review. Quick answers to your bullets: 

- HIPAA / BAA: Redwood supports HIPAA-covered workflows. We are able to sign a Business Associate Agreement — I’ll loop Legal once you confirm standard BAA terms.

- SOC 2: Redwood currently has a SOC 2 Type I report (completed 2025-11) and we are targeting SOC 2 Type II completion in Q4 2026. In the meantime, we can provide the Type I report along with our control matrix and recent penetration test summary.

- Deletion SLAs (summary):
   • User data deletion: our standard is deletion within 30 days for primary and replicated data once deletion is processed.
   • Backups: backups are retained for 45 days by default; backups are stored encrypted and we can support targeted retention shorter than default on a per-contract basis, with an operational lead time to implement.
   • Immutable backups / legal holds: if a legal hold is required, we treat that as an exception and will provide a case-specific plan.
   • Audit/log retention: application-level logs retained 90 days by default; security/audit logs retained 365 days. Longer retention can be arranged as an add-on.

Notes / caveats:
- "Deletion" implies removal from live systems and primary replicas; backups are handled according to the backup retention cycle and may require coordination to scrub/expire copies. We document the deletion timestamp and provide deletion certificates for audit requests where required.
- For HIPAA PHI workflows we recommend a short addendum that specifies any differing retention/deletion workflows for clinical data.

I’ve attached the VSA responses and the retention FAQ. Please let us know which items you want to prioritize. If 30-day deletion for backups is a hard requirement, we’ll flag that as an operational change that needs contract language and an additional commit from infra (Rishi is copied).

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor

Hi Samantha / Neha / Marissa —

Quick operational note from infra/ops on the backup & log points Neha raised: 

- Backups: We run incremental snapshots with a default 45-day retention window; full snapshots are kept for 90 days for disaster recovery. Backups are encrypted at rest. If Amaya requires a 30-day absolute deletion SLA for backups (i.e., backups are expunged within 30 days of a deletion request), that’s possible but will require a dedicated runbook and a contract amendment to reflect the operational change and potential recovery risk. Estimated lead time to implement per-account: 4-6 weeks.

- Log retention: Application logs are available for 90 days; security/audit logs are forwarded to our long-term archive (secure ELK cluster) for 365 days by default. If Amaya needs >365 days we can provision extended retention as part of a paid support add-on.

- Deletion certificate: We can generate a signed deletion certificate that includes timestamps and the systems where deletion occurred.

If this matches your risk appetite, we can capture the 30-day backup deletion SLA in a contract addendum and run a short operational onboarding to document the runbook.

Thanks,
Rishi
